definitions.explanation: Humble form of 言う, used when referring to one's own speech.

examples.japanese: {田中|たなか}と{申|もう}します。
{何|なん}と{申|もう}しましょうか。
ABC{商事|しょうじ}の{鈴木|すずき}と{申|もう}しますが、{山田|やまだ}{様|さま}はいらっしゃいますか。
examples.english: My name is Suzuki from ABC Trading — is Mr. Yamada available?

examples.japanese: {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございませんが、もう{一度|いちど}お{名前|なまえ}をお{聞|き}かせいただけますか。
examples.english: I'm terribly sorry, but could you tell me your name once more?
examples.notes: {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ない = I'm sorry (lit. there's no excuse)

examples.japanese: {先|さき}ほど{担当|たんとう}の{者|もの}が{申|もう}しました{通|とお}り、{来週|らいしゅう}までにご{連絡|れんらく}いたします。
examples.english: As our representative mentioned earlier, we will contact you by next week.
examples.notes: Using {申|もう}す for in-group members when speaking to outsiders

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めまして、{本日|ほんじつ}{司会|しかい}を{務|つと}めます{佐藤|さとう}と{申|もう}します。どうぞよろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。
examples.english: Nice to meet you. My name is Sato, and I will be serving as today's host. Pleased to meet you.

notes:
申す is the humble form of 言う, used to lower oneself when speaking.

CONJUGATION:
- 申します (polite)
- 申して (te-form)
- 申した (past)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- 〜と申します: my name is...
- 申し訳ない: I'm sorry (lit. there's no excuse)

KEIGO TYPE:
- {謙譲語|けんじょうご}: Humble language
- Honorific equivalent: おっしゃる
